title: Quantifying and Attributing Polarization to Annotator Groups

bias_targets.methodology: Calculating the apunim (Aposteriori Unimodality) metric to attribute annotation polarization in toxicity and hate speech datasets to annotator racial and ethnic subgroups (e.g., African American, White, Asian, Latino).

Applying the apunim metric to compare annotation polarization and fundamental disagreements among annotators with varying levels of educational attainment (e.g., High school, Bachelor's, Doctoral degrees).
Measuring annotation polarization attributed to annotators' self-reported importance of religion using the apunim metric to identify trends between highly religious and irreligious annotators.
Quantifying annotation polarization across different generational cohorts (Gen Z, Millennials, Gen X+) and age ranges using the apunim metric.
Evaluating annotation polarization and fundamental disagreements between different annotator gender identities (e.g., men, women, non-binary) using the apunim metric.
Analyzing how annotator political affiliation (Conservative, Independent, Liberal) contributes to dataset-level annotation polarization in toxicity detection.
Using the apunim metric to attribute annotation polarization to annotators of different sexual orientations (Bisexual, Heterosexual, Homosexual).
